Gap
GAP
n. (a breach in a wall; the place an intercessor is to stand)
From Old Norse gap, an opening or chasm. In the Authorized Version it is a breach in a city wall, and both prophetic uses turn it into a figure for intercession — the man who stands where the wall is broken.

Biblical Definition

And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none. The sentence comes at the end of a chapter cataloguing the sins of every class in Jerusalem — princes, priests, prophets, and people of the land — and it is the bleakest line in Ezekiel. God is not looking for an army. He is looking for one man to stand in a breach, and there is not one. The same prophet had already charged the false prophets with the failure: ye have not gone up into the gaps, neither made up the hedge for the house of Israel to stand in the battle in the day of the LORD. The image is a city wall with a hole in it, and the intercessor is the body that fills the hole. Psalm 106 names the man who once did it: had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them. This is why the New Testament's first instruction about public worship is what it is: I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): an opening or breach in a fence or wall; in Scripture, the breach where an intercessor stands between a people and the wrath they have earned.

expand to see more

GAP, n. An opening in anything made by breaking or parting; a breach in a fence or wall.

BREACH, n. The act of breaking; a gap; an opening made by breaking, as in a wall.

HEDGE, n. A fence or inclosure formed of thorn bushes or other shrubs.

INTERCESSION, n. The act of interceding; mediation; interposition between parties at variance.

MEDIATOR, n. One that interposes between parties at variance for the purpose of reconciling them.

Key Scripture

Eze 22:30 — "And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none."

Eze 13:5 — "Ye have not gone up into the gaps, neither made up the hedge for the house of Israel to stand in the battle in the day of the LORD."

Psa 106:23 — "Therefore he said that he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them."

1Ti 2:1 — "I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men;"

Modern Corruption

Intercession is treated as a private devotional comfort for the one praying, when Scripture presents it as a public office performed on behalf of a people under judgment, and names its absence as a reason for ruin.

expand to see more

Ezekiel 22:30 sets prayer in a context most modern treatments avoid entirely. A nation is under sentence, the sentence is deserved, and God searches for a man to stand between the sentence and the people. Intercession here is dangerous, public, and costly: to stand in the gap is to occupy the place the enemy is coming through. Moses did it and offered to be blotted out of God's book instead of Israel; Abraham did it for Sodom, and pressed the number down from fifty to ten; Samuel called it sin to cease from praying for the people. The comforting devotional register has nothing to say to this and was never meant to.

The corruption also runs through the pulpit, and Ezekiel 13 names it there first. The prophets had not gone up into the gaps; they had daubed the wall with untempered morter and said peace where there was no peace. A ministry that will not name the breach cannot stand in it. Christ is the one who finally did: the Mediator between God and men, who ever liveth to make intercession for them, standing in a gap no other man could fill, and the church's praying is the small echo of his great intercession, commanded first of all.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew perets (H6556), a breach or gap; gader (H1447), a wall or hedge; 'amad (H5975), to stand.

expand to see more

Hebrew perets (H6556) — a breach, a break, a gap; stand in the gap before me.

Hebrew gader (H1447) — a wall, a fence, a hedge; make up the hedge.

Hebrew 'amad (H5975) — to stand, to take one's stand; the intercessor's posture.

Hebrew shachath (H7843) — to destroy, to ruin; that I should not destroy it.

Greek enteuxis (G1783) — an intercession, a petition; first of all, intercessions for all men.

Usage

"“stand in the gap before me for the land” — and God found none."

"“Ye have not gone up into the gaps” — the charge against the false prophets."

"“Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach” — the man who did."
